html:
Read this sentence.

The number of commuters who ride bicycles across the city’s bridges have nearly doubled over the past decade.

Which edit should be made to correct this sentence?
exp:
The question asks for the edit that corrects the sentence. The subject of the main verb is the singular noun number, so the verb must be has, not have.

A. Incorrect. Commuters must stay plural: the number of is followed by a plural noun, and the plural verb ride depends on it.

B. CORRECT. The number of always takes a singular verb. The plural nouns commuters, bicycles, and bridges stand between the subject and the verb, but the subject is number: The number … has nearly doubled.

C. Incorrect. Who refers to the plural commuters, so ride is already correct.

D. Incorrect. After the helping verb the past participle doubled is required; have double is not a verb form.

html:
Read this paragraph.

(1) A coral reef, though it resembles a mass of colorful rocks, is built by colonies of tiny animals called polyps. (2) Each of the polyps secretes a hard limestone skeleton that remains long after the animal has died. (3) Living among the branches of the coral are thousands of fish, crabs, and sponges that depend on the reef for shelter. (4) Neither rising water temperatures nor pollution from coastal cities have been easy for these fragile ecosystems to withstand.

Which sentence contains an error in subject-verb agreement?
exp:
The question asks which sentence has a verb that does not agree with its subject. In sentence 4 the subjects are joined by neither … nor, so the verb agrees with the nearer subject, the singular pollution; have been should be has been.

A. Incorrect. In sentence 1 the singular subject reef correctly takes is built, even though a clause separates them.

B. Incorrect. In sentence 2 the subject is the singular Each, not polyps, so secretes is correct.

C. Incorrect. In sentence 3 the subject follows the verb: thousands of fish, crabs, and sponges is plural, so are is correct, and depend agrees with the same plural group.

D. CORRECT. With neither … nor the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. That subject is pollution; the plural cities is only part of the phrase from coastal cities. The sentence should read Neither rising water temperatures nor pollution from coastal cities has been easy.

html:
Read this paragraph.

(1) When the Brooklyn Bridge opened in 1883 its two stone towers, each of which rises more than 270 feet above the river, was taller than nearly every building in New York. (2) John Roebling, the engineer who designed the bridge, died before construction began; his son Washington took over the project. (3) After Washington fell ill, his wife, Emily Roebling, carried his instructions to the workers and oversaw much of the remaining construction. (4) Tens of thousands of vehicles, as well as thousands of pedestrians and cyclists, now cross the bridge each day.

Which pair of revisions need to be made in this paragraph?
opts: Sentence 1: Insert a comma after 1883 AND change was to were.
Sentence 2: Change died to dies AND change the semicolon to a comma.
Sentence 3: Delete the comma after ill AND change oversaw to oversees.
Sentence 4: Change cross to crosses AND delete the comma after cyclists.
exp:
The question asks which sentence contains two errors that the paired revisions would fix. Sentence 1 needs a comma after the introductory clause When the Brooklyn Bridge opened in 1883, and its plural subject towers needs the plural verb were.

A. CORRECT. The opening dependent clause must be set off with a comma after 1883. The subject of the main clause is towers; the clause each of which rises more than 270 feet above the river has its own singular subject and verb, but it does not change the main subject, so was must become were.

B. Incorrect. Died correctly matches the past-tense verbs around it, and the semicolon correctly joins two complete sentences; a comma there would create a run-on.

C. Incorrect. The comma after ill correctly follows an introductory clause, and oversaw correctly matches the past-tense carried.

D. Incorrect. The subject is the plural Tens of thousands of vehicles, so cross is correct; the phrase beginning as well as is an interruption that needs a comma on both sides.

html:
Read this sentence.

Among the artifacts recovered from the sunken merchant ship was a bronze compass, several glass bottles, and a chest of silver coins.

Which edit should be made to correct this sentence?
exp:
The question asks for the edit that corrects the sentence. The sentence is inverted: its subject comes after the verb and is the compound a bronze compass, several glass bottles, and a chest of silver coins, which requires the plural verb were.

A. Incorrect. Among requires a plural object, so artifacts is correct; it is also not the subject of the sentence.

B. Incorrect. Recovered is a participle describing the artifacts, not the main verb; recovers would make no sense.

C. CORRECT. Turn the sentence around to find the subject: A bronze compass, several glass bottles, and a chest of silver coins were among the artifacts. Three items joined by and are plural, even though the first item, a bronze compass, is singular and sits next to the verb.

D. Incorrect. The comma after compass separates items in a series and must stay.

html:
Read this paragraph.

(1) A colony of honeybees, which may contain as many as 60,000 insects, depend on a single queen to lay all of its eggs. (2) The workers, each of which lives only a few weeks in summer, gather nectar and build the wax comb. (3) There are also a few hundred drones, male bees whose only task is to mate with a queen. (4) The number of bees in a hive rises through the spring and reaches its peak in early summer.

Which sentence contains an error in subject-verb agreement?
exp:
The question asks which sentence has a verb that does not agree with its subject. In sentence 1 the subject is the singular noun colony, so depend should be depends.

A. CORRECT. The subject colony is singular, as the pronoun its later in the sentence confirms. The plural nouns honeybees and insects come between the subject and the verb, but the sentence should read A colony … depends on a single queen.

B. Incorrect. In sentence 2 the plural subject workers correctly takes gather and build; inside the interrupting clause, the singular each correctly takes lives.

C. Incorrect. In sentence 3 the subject follows the verb: a few hundred drones is plural, so There are is correct, and the singular task correctly takes is.

D. Incorrect. In sentence 4 The number is singular, so rises and reaches are correct even though the plural bees stands beside them.

html:
Read this paragraph.

(1) Every spring, the students at Lincoln Middle School hold a science fair in the gymnasium. (2) Each of the projects is judged by a panel of teachers, and the winners receive ribbons. (3) This year, neither the judges nor the principal were prepared for the size of the crowd, and there was not enough chairs for half of the visitors. (4) A team of eighth graders, along with their science teacher, has offered to plan next year’s event.

Which pair of revisions need to be made in this paragraph?
opts: Sentence 1: Change students to student’s AND change hold to holds.
Sentence 2: Change is to are AND delete the comma after teachers.
Sentence 3: Change were to was AND change there was to there were.
Sentence 4: Change has to have AND delete the comma after teacher.
exp:
The question asks which sentence contains two errors that the paired revisions would fix. Sentence 3 has two verbs that disagree with their subjects: were should be was to agree with principal, and there was should be there were to agree with chairs.

A. Incorrect. Students is a plural subject, not a possessive, and it correctly takes the plural verb hold.

B. Incorrect. The subject Each is singular, so is judged is correct, and the comma before and correctly separates two complete sentences.

C. CORRECT. With neither … nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject, the singular principal: neither the judges nor the principal was prepared. After there, the verb agrees with the noun that follows it, the plural chairs: there were not enough chairs.

D. Incorrect. The subject is the singular team; the phrase along with their science teacher does not make it plural, so has offered is correct, and the interrupting phrase needs a comma on both sides.

html:
Read this sentence.

Each of the murals that decorate the walls of the subway station depict a scene from the neighborhood’s history.

Which edit should be made to correct this sentence?
exp:
The question asks for the edit that corrects the sentence. The subject of the main verb is the singular pronoun Each, so the verb must be depicts.

A. Incorrect. Each of the must be followed by a plural noun, so murals is correct.

B. Incorrect. That refers to the plural murals, so decorate is already correct.

C. Incorrect. Nothing is wrong with walls, and changing it would not repair the verb.

D. CORRECT. Remove the words between the subject and the verb and the error is plain: Each … depicts a scene. The plural verb decorate earlier in the sentence belongs to murals, not to Each.

html:
Read this paragraph.

(1) The New York City Marathon, which winds through all five boroughs, attracts more than 50,000 runners each November. (2) Lining the streets along the 26.2-mile course is more than a million spectators, many of whom arrive hours before the first runners pass. (3) The crew of volunteers at each aid station hands out water and sports drinks to the runners. (4) Neither the steep bridges nor the unpredictable autumn weather discourages the thousands of people who apply for a place in the race each year.

Which sentence contains an error in subject-verb agreement?
exp:
The question asks which sentence has a verb that does not agree with its subject. Sentence 2 is inverted: its subject, more than a million spectators, follows the verb and is plural, so is should be are.

A. Incorrect. In sentence 1 the singular subject Marathon correctly takes attracts, and which, referring to the Marathon, correctly takes winds.

B. CORRECT. Turn the sentence around to find the subject: More than a million spectators are lining the streets. The singular noun course just before the verb is part of the phrase along the 26.2-mile course, not the subject.

C. Incorrect. In sentence 3 the subject is the singular crew, so hands is correct even though volunteers is plural.

D. Incorrect. In sentence 4 the verb agrees with the nearer subject after nor, the singular weather, so discourages is correct; who refers to the plural people, so apply is correct.

html:
Read this paragraph.

(1) The Metropolitan Museum of Art, one of the largest museums in the world, houses more than a million works. (2) Its collection of Egyptian artifacts includes the Temple of Dendur, which was shipped to New York in pieces. (3) There are also galleries devoted to armor, musical instruments, and photography. (4) Each of the museum’s seventeen departments employ curators; who decide which objects are displayed.

Which pair of revisions need to be made in this paragraph?
opts: Sentence 1: Delete the comma after Art AND change houses to house.
Sentence 2: Change includes to include AND change was to were.
Sentence 3: Change are to is AND delete the comma after armor.
Sentence 4: Change employ to employs AND change the semicolon to a comma.
exp:
The question asks which sentence contains two errors that the paired revisions would fix. In sentence 4 the singular subject Each needs the verb employs, and the semicolon is wrong because who decide which objects are displayed is not a complete sentence.

A. Incorrect. The commas around one of the largest museums in the world correctly set off an interrupting phrase, and the singular subject Museum correctly takes houses.

B. Incorrect. The subject collection is singular, so includes is correct, and which refers to the singular Temple of Dendur, so was shipped is correct.

C. Incorrect. The subject follows the verb: galleries is plural, so There are is correct, and the comma after armor separates items in a series.

D. CORRECT. Each is singular no matter how many departments follow it: Each … employs curators. A semicolon must have a complete sentence on both sides, and the clause beginning with who cannot stand alone, so a comma is needed. Decide is correct because who refers to the plural curators.

html:
Read this sentence.

The lead violinist, as well as the three cellists who sit beside her, have been invited to perform at the citywide festival next month.

Which edit should be made to correct this sentence?
exp:
The question asks for the edit that corrects the sentence. The subject is the singular violinist; a phrase beginning with as well as does not make the subject plural, so the verb must be has.

A. CORRECT. Unlike and, the words as well as do not create a compound subject. The phrase between the commas can be lifted out, leaving The lead violinist … has been invited.

B. Incorrect. Who refers to the plural cellists, so sit is already correct.

C. Incorrect. Three requires the plural cellists.

D. Incorrect. The interrupting phrase needs a comma at each end; deleting the second one would leave it unclosed.

html:
Read this paragraph.

(1) Completed in 1825, the Erie Canal connects the Hudson River to Lake Erie. (2) The system of locks along the route raises and lowers boats over a climb of more than 500 feet between Albany and Buffalo. (3) The cost of shipping grain and other goods from the Midwest to New York City were reduced by nearly ninety percent once the canal opened. (4) There were few engineers in the country with any experience in building canals, so many of the workers learned their trade on the job.

Which sentence contains an error in subject-verb agreement?
exp:
The question asks which sentence has a verb that does not agree with its subject. In sentence 3 the subject is the singular noun cost, so were reduced should be was reduced.

A. Incorrect. In sentence 1 the singular subject Erie Canal correctly takes connects.

B. Incorrect. In sentence 2 the subject is the singular system, so raises and lowers is correct even though locks is plural.

C. CORRECT. Everything between cost and the verb, including the plural goods, belongs to the phrase of shipping grain and other goods from the Midwest to New York City. The sentence should read The cost … was reduced.

D. Incorrect. In sentence 4 the subject follows the verb: few engineers is plural, so There were is correct, and the plural many of the workers correctly takes learned.

html:
Read this sentence.

Either the coach or the two team captains decides which players will start, and the list of starters is posted outside the gym every Friday.

Which edit should be made to correct this sentence?
exp:
The question asks for the edit that corrects the sentence. When subjects are joined by either … or, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, here the plural captains, so the verb must be decide.

A. Incorrect. Two requires the plural captains.

B. CORRECT. The subject closer to the verb is the two team captains, so the plural decide is needed: Either the coach or the two team captains decide. The singular coach is farther from the verb and does not control it.

C. Incorrect. The subject of the second clause is the singular list, not starters, so is posted is correct.

D. Incorrect. After the helping verb will, the base form start is required.
